When describing traumatic events people often say, "Everything seemed to go in slow motion..." Have there been any studies conducted or any theories that explain this perception?

Don't quote me on this, I may be wrong, but I believe it has something to do with your "fight or flight" response.

When you're in danger, your body automatically pumps you up full of adrenaline, which in turn may speed up your reactions. This may be the cause of the perception of time slowing down. It's just your body reacting much faster than usual to either avoid as much danger as possible or to help prevent as much damage as possible to vital organs.

I remember reading an article a couple years ago (Sorry, no way I'm going to be able to find a link) that basically stated in the situation, your perception of time remains the same. However, because a traumatic event or moment of extreme excitement (bungee jumping, skydiving etc) is so notable to the brain that it becomes hyper aware of what's going on, so your ability to recall more minute details is increased. More information = the illusion that time slowed down.

Edit: Found the article in question. Published in 2007. Take it with a grain of salt.

Someone made an experiment to test whether the world really "slowed down" or if it was just a placebo thingy.

They did this through getting hold of a bunch of subjects that had an intense fear of hights and then throwing them in free fall, only to be catched by a large net a few seconds later. The subjects were equipped with a wrist watch that was blinking in a rate that made the subject unable to read the time. A slowing down effect on the sucjects mind was predicted to have the subject able to read the time during the seconds of free falling in terror.

The slowing down effect turned out to be very real indeed.

A friend forwarded this to me today and I thought you guys might enjoy. Not sure I agree with 100% of the content, but it's an interesting take on the multi-verse hypothesis in relationship with the fine-tuning argument.

I call "Fine-tuning" arguments "Benny Hill's Glasses" arguments.

Benny Hill once did a bit (he was a comedian) where, as a preacher, he said "when God made man, glasses hadn't been invented yet, but look where he put our noses."

The idea being god was so omniscient, he made our face to fit the glasses he knew we'd make.

Of course, in reality, we made glasses to fit the face we had...and if our faces were different, so would be our glasses.

"Fine-tuning" is a lot like that - assuming everything was "designed" to fit current life...rather than realizing current life evolved to fit how things were "designed..."
